title: A-level Maths: Differentiation from first principles
subtitle: Pure Maths Year 1, Chapter 12 — the gradient of a curve

nodes.label: Speed as a gradient
nodes.summary: On a distance-time graph, speed is how steep the graph is. Between two times, average speed = distance travelled / time taken.

quiz.question: A car is 1 m from the start at t = 1 s and 9 m from the start at t = 3 s. What is its average speed?
quiz.explanation: It travels 9 - 1 = 8 m in 3 - 1 = 2 s, so 8 / 2 = 4 m/s.

nodes.label: Gradient of a straight line
nodes.summary: Gradient m = rise / run = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1). A straight line has the same gradient everywhere.

quiz.question: What is the gradient of the line through (0, 1) and (2, 7)?

nodes.label: Gradient of a chord
nodes.summary: A chord joins two points on a curve. Its gradient is the average gradient of the curve between those points, not the gradient at either point.

quiz.question: On y = x^2, what is the gradient of the chord from (1, 1) to (2, 4)?
quiz.explanation: Rise 4 - 1 = 3, run 2 - 1 = 1, so the gradient is 3.

nodes.label: Tangent as the limit of chords
nodes.summary: Keep P fixed and slide Q towards it (Q is h to the right of P). As h -> 0 the chord's gradient approaches the gradient of the tangent at P. On y = x^2 at x = 1: h = 1 gives 3, h = 0.1 gives 2.1, h = 0.01 gives 2.01 -> 2.

quiz.question: On y = x^2, the chord from x = 1 to x = 1 + h has gradient 2 + h. What is it when h = 0.001?
quiz.explanation: 2 + 0.001 = 2.001. As h gets smaller it gets closer to 2, the gradient of the tangent.

nodes.label: Differentiation from first principles
nodes.summary: Gradient of y = x^2 at x: ((x + h)^2 - x^2) / h = (2xh + h^2) / h = 2x + h, which tends to 2x as h -> 0. So dy/dx = 2x.

quiz.question: What is the gradient of y = x^2 at x = 3?
quiz.explanation: dy/dx = 2x, so at x = 3 the gradient is 2 × 3 = 6.
